author: Juliet Renford
summary: Emily Henry-style contemporary romance with the emphasis on small-town and found-family warmth: a big-city heroine lands in a quirky small town, gets adopted by its eccentric residents, and falls for someone who belongs there. Of the three Endless Tales Emily Henry voices, Juliet Renford is the coziest; the wit is still sharp, but community, rituals, and belonging carry the story.
sentences: Mostly 8-18 words with a lively, observational rhythm; comic lists of town details; an occasional long, warm sentence when the heroine falls for the place.
pacing: Medium; scenes alternate between romance beats and community set pieces (a festival, a book club, a town meeting gone wrong). Time moves over a summer or a season.
vocabulary: Contemporary, witty, affectionate; specific local color (bait shop, diner pie case, the one stoplight). No snobbish put-downs, no crude language.
dialogue: About 55%. Banter between the leads plus a chorus of colorful townspeople with distinct speech habits; dialogue reveals kindness behind gruffness. Clear tags for audio, with each townsperson named on their first line.
narration: First person past from a heroine who arrives a little lonely and judgmental and narrates her own thawing with humor. Notices people's rituals and small kindnesses; mentions her old city life only for contrast.
openings: Opens with a sharp, funny line about arriving somewhere she didn't plan to be, then a first encounter with a local who already knows her business.
scene_endings: Ends on a warm community beat or a quiet romantic moment, with a gentle laugh.

ending.type: Happily ever after with found family
ending.finale: The heroine chooses to stay, or to make a place for herself, and the whole town shows up for the declaration. The last image is a town ritual she is now part of.
ending.episode: Ends on a jolt: news that a beloved town spot will close, the hero's surprising past emerging, or her old life calling with an offer she can't easily refuse.

signature_moves: An ensemble of eccentric locals with running gags
Town rituals (festival, trivia night, Sunday supper) as story anchors
Outsider heroine slowly learning everyone's names and stories
Banter with a love interest everyone adores except her, at first
Found family stepping in where blood family failed
Closed-door romance; the big kiss happens in public or at the door
avoid: Too many named characters in one scene for audio
AI cliches like 'a tapestry of community'
samples: Within an hour of arriving in Bramble Hollow, three facts became clear: the town had one stoplight, nobody obeyed it, and every person in the diner already knew my name. "You're the new librarian," said the waitress, Dot, setting down a pie I hadn't ordered. "Interim," I said. "Six weeks." "Sure, honey." At the counter, a man in a flannel shirt snorted into his coffee. "They all say six weeks," he said, without looking up.

"Is it always like this?" I asked. The whole town was crammed onto the lawn behind the firehouse, someone's uncle was tuning a fiddle badly, and four children were attempting to steal a pie off the judging table. Sam handed me a paper cup of lemonade. "No," he said. "Usually it's louder." Dot waved at us from across the lawn, then mimed something that looked suspiciously like a kiss, and I became very interested in my lemonade.
